13
 and
 spatial
 working
 memory
 test
 scores.
 At
 transfer
 of
 learning
(run
 13),
 young
 adults
 with
 higher
 scores
 on
 the
 Corsi
 block
 back-
wards
 demonstrated
 shorter
 RT
 (r
 =
 −.70,
 df
 =
 16,
 p >
 .01).
 Young
adults
 with
 shorter
 RT
 at
 initial
 learning
 also
 had
 lower
 average
 IEE
(r
 =
 .54,
 df
 =
 18,
 p
 =
 .02).
 Taken
 together,
 these
 results
 indicate
 that
young
 adults
 with
 better
 spatial
 working
 memory
 performance
 as
well
 as
 shorter
 RT
 performed
 better
 at
 both
 motor
 learning
 and
transfer.
 There
 were
 no
 signiﬁcant
 differences
 between
 these
 cor-
relations
 at
 initial
 learning
 versus
 at
 transfer
 in
 the
 young
 adult
group,
 suggesting
 that
 working
 memory
 plays
 a
 role
 in
 both
 pro-
cesses
 for
 this
 age
 group.
 In
 contrast
 to
 young
 adults,
 better
 SWM
performance
 in
 older
 adults
 was
 related
 to
 longer
 RT
 at
 transfer.
That
 is,
 older
 adults
 that
 did
 well
 on
 the
 Corsi
 block
 forward
 or
 the
card
 rotation
 task
 progressively
 increased
 their
 RT
 (Corsi,
 r =
 .55,
 =
 17,
 p
 =
 .02)
 or
 had
 longer
 average
 RT
 at
 initial
 transfer
 (card,
r
 =
 .48,
 df
 =
 17,
 p
 =
 .05).
 RT,
 however,
 was
 not
 related
 to
 other
 visuo-
motor
 adaptation
 performance
 measures
 for
 the
 older
 adults.
Previous
 work
 in
 our
 laboratory
 has
 shown
 that
 SWM
 skills
 are
beneﬁcial
 to
 young
 adults
 during
 early
 learning
 of
 a
 visuomotor
adaptation
 task
 [12].
 We used
 the
 same
 spatial
 control
 and
 SWM
task
 as
 those
 used
 in
 Anguera
 et
 al.
 [12,16]
 studies
 to
 examine
contributions
 of
 SWM
 to
 initial
 learning
 and
 transfer
 here.
 Young
adults
 that
 had
 the
 greatest
 decline
 in
 IEE
 in
 the
 visuomotor
 adap-
tation
 task
 at
 transfer
 of
 learning
 demonstrated
 greater
 accuracy
 in
the
 SWM
 task
 (r
 =
 −54,
 df
 =
 16,
 p
 =
 .03).
 This
 reinforces
 the
 previous
observation
 from
 the
 neuropsychological
 data
 that
 young
 adults
with
 better
 SWM
 performance
 learn
 and
 transfer
 the
 visuomotor
adaptation
 task
 faster.
